# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place

blocks.text:
All targeted tests green. Now deep review of the actual code for remaining issues. Let me examine full new files and relevant existing code:

1. `_scanSegmentStreamed` — check details:
   - `SessionLineScanner(fs: fs, path: segmentPath).scan(...)` — fine.
   - batchFirstLineNumber drift: minor.
   - Note: the rewrite copies good spans via decode/encode. OK.
   - `rewriteMs` set from `phaseSw.elapsedMilliseconds` which started at scan start — so rewriteMs includes read time. Minor reporting inaccuracy. Actually `readMs = phaseSw.elapsedMilliseconds` after flushBatch, then rewrite happens, and `rewriteMs = phaseSw.elapsedMilliseconds` — that's cumulative elapsed since scan start, not rewrite duration. Minor logging inaccuracy. Suggestion-level nit at best.

2. `_openStreamedLocked`: `latestGiantCustoms` — after the loop, full parse of each raw line via `parseSessionEntryLine(rawLine, filePath, 0)`. The line number arg 0 — parse errors would report line 0. Minor.

3. Backstop check for parts: per-segment 2 GiB. OK.

4. `defaultMaxFullOpenBytes = 2 << 30` — actually 2 GiB = 2147483648. `2 << 30` = 2 * 2^30 = 2 GiB. Yes.

5. `SessionLineScanner.scan` — `carry = BytesBuilder(copy: false)`; per-line `carry.toBytes()` then reassign. Fine. `carry.isNotEmpty` — BytesBuilder has isNotEmpty. OK.

6. Edge: a chunk boundary mid-line; sublist per line — O(n²)? `carry.add(chunk.sublist(lineStart, i))` copies; each line's bytes copied ~twice. For a 2 GiB file with small lines, chunk.sublist per line copies each byte once into carry, then toBytes copies again. Acceptable.

7. Performance concern: in `_scanSegmentStreamed`, the batch weight: `batchLines.fold<int>(0, (n, l) => n + l.length)` — O(batch) each line added → O(batch²) per batch ≈ 500² = 250k char-length ops per batch — fine.

8. `repairSessionLedgers`: After pass 1, `keptSpans.addAll(latestByType.values)` then sort. But `_appendSpan` coalesced keptSpans; adding latest spans after could create overlap? No — latest spans were excluded from keptSpans (returned before `_appendSpan`). Sorting gives file order. Correct.

   But wait — `recordsKept = keptSpans.length` — after coalescing; equals the count of kept lines only if spans are 1:1 with lines... `_appendSpan` merges contiguous spans, so keptSpans.length ≤ kept line count. recordsKept is thus the merged span count, not the record count. The report says "recordsKept" and summary prints "$recordsKept kept". Slightly inaccurate when contiguous lines coalesce (the common case! consecutive kept lines merge into one span). Hmm, actually let me re-check the scan callback: for kept lines it calls `_appendSpan(goodSpans, span)` — consecutive kept lines coalesce into a single span. So keptSpans.length undercounts records. `recordsRead` counts lines. So "records read: 10, kept: 3" could print when 10 records were read and 8 kept contiguously (one span). That's a real (cosmetic) reporting bug worth flagging. Let me verify: in `repairSessionLedgers`, `var recordsRead = 0;` incremented per non-blank line. Kept lines go through `_appendSpan(keptSpans, span)` — coalesced. So yes, recordsKept is span-count. In the dry-run summary "10 records read, 3 kept" would be wrong (8 actually kept).

   Wait, let me double check the test: seedSession writes header + 5 custom ledger lines + 1 message. Repair: all 5 customs dropped, message kept → keptSpans = [message span] → recordsKept = 1. recordsRead = 6? Summary line: "6 records read, 1 kept" — accurate there because dropped lines break contiguity. But in a dry-run of a healthy session with 100 contiguous message lines: recordsRead=100, kept=1 span. Report would say "1 kept". Misleading. Severity: IMPORTANT? It's a user-facing report accuracy issue in a brand-new command whose whole purpose is reporting. I'd say SUGGESTION-to-IMPORTANT. The dry-run report is what users use to decide. I'll classify as IMPORTANT-lite... Actually the counting is genuinely wrong for the primary use case (dry-run on a bloated file with mostly-kept conversation lines): "kept" would show tiny numbers. Users may misread "dropped" from recordsRead - recordsKept. I'll rate IMPORTANT.

   Hmm wait — actually let me recheck: are contiguous spans actually merged in repair? `_appendSpan(keptSpans, span)` — yes, merges when `spans.last.$2 == span.$1`. Consecutive kept lines → one span. So recordsKept == number of spans, not records. Confirmed bug (cosmetic but user-facing).

9. `_liveRowForPath` calls `repo.list()` — full listing; fine.

10. `session_repair_command.dart`: by-id path — `resolveRepairableSession` lists sessions and calls `repo.sessionNameQuick(metadata)` for each — check exists. Also note: by-id path does NOT verify the file exists before repair; repairSessionLedgers stats and fails with notFound — handled.

11. Live guard: presenceStore staleness — `list()` auto-drops stale heartbeats (15s). OK.

12. Repair + rotation: a session that has `.part-NN` segments! `repairSessionLedgers` repairs only the given path (primary). But the bloat may live in the rotated `.part-NN` segments (rotation moves older records into parts). The repair drops ledger records from the primary only; the parts still hold giant ledger lines. After repair, open loads parts oldest-first — still streams them (bounded), but the file size problem persists — the total across segments may still exceed 2 GiB, and the per-segment backstop only refuses > 2 GiB per segment. Total = parts + primary each < 2 GiB but sum > 2 GiB → open proceeds, streaming handles it (bounded memory). So not a memory issue, but the repair command's promise ("shrink the ledger") doesn't address parts: the giant ledger records in `.part-NN` files survive the repair and the session file set stays bloated. Does the error message "shrink the ledger with `fa session repair`" help when the primary is small but parts are huge? The tooLarge refusal only triggers per-segment. So a session whose primary is 100 MB but parts total 12 GiB never refuses and streams fine — bounded memory, just slow. Hmm, streaming 12 GiB in 4 MiB chunks = ~3000 reads — OK.

    But also: does repair consider that the LATEST shell_job_registry snapshot may live in a part segment? If the primary contains zero `shell_job_registry` records (all rotated to parts), repair keeps none, and resume rehydration finds nothing — job board empty. That's semantically fine (registry is best-effort). And model_request_summary in parts are replay-only. So acceptable, but worth a SUGGESTION: repair should mention/handle `.part-NN` siblings (at minimum warn that rotated segments were not scanned, or repair them too).

    Actually wait — is there a correctness issue? `fa session repair <id>` resolves the session primary path. Rotation parts are siblings `<path>.part-NN`. Repair doesn't touch them. Fine but incomplete w.r.t. the ticket's goal (the 12.4 GiB file had no rotation, probably). SUGGESTION.

13. In `_openLocked`, the stat retry: `retryTransientSessionIo(() => fs.fileInfo(filePath), op: 'open', ...)`. Then for the streamed path, primaryFileSize is passed. Between the heal and the stat — heal ran before stat. Good ordering as documented.

14. `_openStreamedLocked` — after scanning, it fully parses latest giant customs. Note: `parseSessionEntryLine(rawLine, filePath, 0)` — could throw on a malformed giant line (it was parsed shallow OK but full parse fails?). If shallow parse said it's a valid custom record (header decoded), full parse should succeed too... unless the payload JSON is malformed but header fine. Shallow decode uses `parseShallowCustomRecord` which checks the header; the full decode could fail on bad payload JSON. Then open throws SessionException — whole open fails where the whole-file path might have... the whole-file path parses all lines with parseSessionEntryLine too, failing similarly. Consistent.

15. Timing: `parseMs` only counts giant-custom rehydration; batch parsing happens inside flushBatch during scan (counted in readMs window since phaseSw covers scan until readMs snapshot). Mislabeled but harmless.

16. `agent_hub_cli.dart` `_persistJobBoard`: `_persistChain.then((_) async {...})` — with `on Object` catch inside?…

Part files are `<primary>.part-0001` — they do NOT end in `.jsonl`, so the repair CLI's path branch (`target.endsWith('.jsonl')`) refuses... actually no — the by-id branch resolves metadata.path (primary). The path branch accepts only `.jsonl`-suffixed targets; a user cannot point repair at a `.part-NN` file via the CLI at all (`session repair: no such file` → actually it first checks `env.exists(target)` — the part exists, but since it doesn't end with `.jsonl` it goes to the by-id branch → "session not found"). So rotated segments can never be repaired via the CLI. A rotated session whose parts hold the bloat stays bloated, and the `tooLarge` error message points at `fa session repair` as the rescue path — which won't shrink the parts.

How severe? The tooLarge refusal fires per-segment (>2 GiB). If a `.part-NN` exceeds 2 GiB, the user is told to run `fa session repair`, which only rewrites the primary — the part remains > 2 GiB and open still refuses. The rescue path named in the error is a dead end for exactly that case. That's a functional gap worth IMPORTANT (docs/hint overpromise; also repair could iterate parts). Though — memory-wise the streamed open handles big-but-under-2GiB segments fine; the refusal is only per-segment >2GiB. The 12.4 GiB ticket session was a single unrotated file. Rotation only kicks in at kSessionSegmentRotateBytes — let me check the value.
{"command":"grep -n \"kSessionSegmentRotateBytes\" lib/src/session/session_storage.dart | head -3; sed -n 384,400p lib/src/session/session_storage.dart"}

Rotation caps segments at ~95 MB, so a `.part-NN` can never approach the 2 GiB backstop — per-segment refusal on parts can't realistically trigger. So the `tooLarge` refusal realistically only fires on the primary, and repair targets exactly the primary. The rotation-gap concern is thus minor: parts stay ≤95 MB each, total across many parts can be GiBs but the streamed open handles that in bounded memory. So repair ignoring parts means post-repair open still streams all parts — correct, just not smaller. The error hint remains valid for the realistic case. I'll downgrade this to a SUGGESTION (repair could optionally compact parts / note in help that rotated segments are untouched).

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1247 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1247 - **Title**: gh-1073 Session JSONL grows unboundedly (12 GiB ledger records) → resume fails with 'Failed to read session' + heap-exhaustion crash - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1073` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 30 - **Additions**: +2562 - **Deletions**: -54 - **Created**: 2026-10-04T21:28:28Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-05T00:21:12Z ## PR Description ### What changed Bounded the session-JSONL growth that grew a month-long session to 12.4 GiB and made open/resume safe for huge files: ledger payloads are capped and deduped at the write site, the full open streams the file in bounded chunks (never one giant `String`) with a 2 GiB hard backstop, and a new `fa session repair` command rewrites bloated JSONLs. This leg fixed the last review leftovers: one analyzer lint and two stale retry-test assertions that still counted the old `readTextFile` open surface (the open now stats + streams, so the counters read `statCalls`). ### Key decisions - `ledger_caps.dart`: 300-char cap on every string field in `shell_job_registry` / `subagent_registry` records + `LedgerSnapshotDeduper` skips byte-identical snapshots at the write site - `model_request_summary`: per-message summaries capped (newest 64 messages / 256 KB budget); older messages degrade to role+chars stubs — record still describes the whole request - `JsonlSessionStorage._openLocked`: stat-first, refuse >2 GiB with a named `tooLarge` `SessionException` pointing at windowed resume / `fa session repair`; ranged filesystems get a fully streamed line-scan parse with header-only decode of giant `custom` ledgers (only the latest per `customType` is fully parsed — exactly what resume rehydration reads) - `session_repair.dart` + CLI: drop replay-only ledger types, keep-latest for snapshot registries, conservative (unknown/unparseable lines kept), backup + `--dry-run` ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/session test/trajectory test/task test/cli ``` Full core suite (`dart test --exclude-tags integration`): 7960 passed / 16 skipped. The 3 failures in `providers_queue_editor_test.dart` are environmental — the CI shell leaks `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`, which the editor correctly refuses to override (all 13 pass with the var unset). A pre-existing glibc heap-corruption abort in the PTY-harness teardown also reproduces on the base commit and is unrelated.
Architecture diagram ```mermaid flowchart TD OPEN[Session open] --> STAT[fileInfo stat] STAT -->|> 2 GiB| REFUSE[tooLarge SessionException] REFUSE --> HINT[windowed resume / fa session repair] STAT -->|<= 2 GiB| STREAM[streamed line scan
bounded chunks] STREAM --> HDR[header-only decode
of giant custom ledgers] HDR --> LATEST[fully parse latest
record per customType] WRITE[ledger writes] --> CAP[ledger_caps: 300-char field cap] CAP --> DEDUP[skip identical snapshots] REPAIR[fa session repair] --> REWRITE[drop replay-only ledgers
keep-latest registries + backup] ```

# gh-1073: Session JSONL grows unboundedly (12 GiB ledger records) → resume fails with 'Failed to read session' + heap-exhaustion crash

## Description

## Session file grows unboundedly (12 GiB) → resume fails with `SessionException: Failed to read session`, then Dart VM OOM crash

### Observed (live, 2026-09-29)

A month-long CLI session (`2026-09-07…01a07bce-….jsonl`) grew to **12.4 GiB / 96,776 lines**. Messages themselves are only ~17 MB; 99.9 % of the file is `custom` ledger records:

| customType | records | total | avg |
|---|---|---|---|
| `model_request_summary` | 18,753 | 9.08 GB | ~484 KB |
| `shell_job_registry` | 29,348 | 3.65 GB | ~124 KB |
| `subagent_registry` | 3,588 | 0.5 GB | ~140 KB |

Resuming the session fails:

```
error: failed to open session 01a07bce-…: SessionException: Failed to read session …/2026-09-07…_01a07bce….jsonl
```

and the process then crashes hard:

```
Exhausted heap space, trying to allocate 25575341936 bytes
```

### Root cause

1. **Unbounded append-only ledgers.**
   - `shell_job_registry` (`lib/src/cli/agent_hub_cli.dart`, `_persistJobBoard`): every job-board mutation appends a **full snapshot of all job cards** (commands, cwd, log tails). ~29k snapshots over the session lifetime; no cap, no dedup, no rotation.
   - `model_request_summary` (`lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`, `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_blobs.dart`): written before **every** model request and embeds a per-message summary of the whole outbound context (`messageCount` reached 1030+). Growth is superlinear: the longer the session, the bigger each record.

2. **Open path reads the whole file into one String.**
   `JsonlSessionStorage._openLocked` (`lib/src/session/session_storage.dart`) calls `fs.readTextFile(filePath)` on the entire JSONL. A 12.4 GiB UTF-8 file becomes a Dart UTF-16 `String` (~25 GB) → heap exhaustion; the wrapped `Failed to read session` error surfaces first, the retry then kills the VM.

   Note: faster/bounded parsing already exists (`SessionParseExecutor` header-only decode for big ledger payloads, `windowed_session_storage.dart`), but it only kicks in **after** the full-file `readTextFile`, so it cannot help here.

### Suggested fix directions

- **Streamed/windowed open**: read the JSONL line-by-line (or in bounded chunks) during open; never materialize the whole file as a single `String`. The header parse already only needs the first line.
- **Cap/rotate ledger records**:
  - `shell_job_registry`: keep only the latest snapshot (supersede prior records, e.g. tombstone/compact or a sidecar), or truncate job card payloads (log tails) before persisting.
  - `model_request_summary`: cap the per-message summary (max messages / max chars), and/or persist it only when the trajectory actually needs replay data.
- **Hard backstop**: refuse to full-read session files above a threshold (e.g. 1–2 GB) with a clear error pointing at a repair/`--shallow` resume path, instead of OOM-crashing.
- **Repair path**: a tool/command that rewrites a bloated JSONL, dropping or trimming `custom` ledgers, so users can rescue long-running sessions.

### Workaround for affected users

Copy the JSONL, strip `custom`-type lines (they are not needed to resume the conversation itself), and resume the copy — or start a new session.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/S…

   - `rewriteMs` set from `phaseSw.elapsedMilliseconds` which started at scan start — so rewriteMs includes read time. Minor reporting inaccuracy. Actually `readMs = phaseSw.elapsedMilliseconds` after flushBatch, then rewrite happens, and `rewriteMs = phaseSw.elapsedMilliseconds` — that's cumulative elapsed since scan start, not rewrite duration. Minor logging inaccuracy. Suggestion-level nit at best.

2. `_openStreamedLocked`: `latestGiantCustoms` — after the loop, full parse of each raw line via `parseSessionEntryLine(rawLine, filePath, 0)`. The line number arg 0 — parse errors would report line 0. Minor.

3. Backstop check for parts: per-segment 2 GiB. OK.

4. `defaultMaxFullOpenBytes = 2 << 30` — actually 2 GiB = 2147483648. `2 << 30` = 2 * 2^30 = 2 GiB. Yes.

5. `SessionLineScanner.scan` — `carry = BytesBuilder(copy: false)`; per-line `carry.toBytes()` then reassign. Fine. `carry.isNotEmpty` — BytesBuilder has isNotEmpty. OK.

6. Edge: a chunk boundary mid-line; sublist per line — O(n²)? `carry.add(chunk.sublist(lineStart, i))` copies; each line's bytes copied ~twice. For a 2 GiB file with small lines, chunk.sublist per line copies each byte once into carry, then toBytes copies again. Acceptable.

7. Performance concern: in `_scanSegmentStreamed`, the batch weight: `batchLines.fold<int>(0, (n, l) => n + l.length)` — O(batch) each line added → O(batch²) per batch ≈ 500² = 250k char-length ops per batch — fine.

8. `repairSessionLedgers`: After pass 1, `keptSpans.addAll(latestByType.values)` then sort. But `_appendSpan` coalesced keptSpans; adding latest spans after could create overlap? No — latest spans were excluded from keptSpans (returned before `_appendSpan`). Sorting gives file order. Correct.

The report says "recordsKept" and summary prints "$recordsKept kept". Slightly inaccurate when contiguous lines coalesce (the common case! consecutive kept lines merge into one span). Hmm, actually let me re-check the scan callback: for kept lines it calls `_appendSpan(goodSpans, span)` — consecutive kept lines coalesce into a single span. So keptSpans.length undercounts records. `recordsRead` counts lines. So "records read: 10, kept: 3" could print when 10 records were read and 8 kept contiguously (one span). That's a real (cosmetic) reporting bug worth flagging. Let me verify: in `repairSessionLedgers`, `var recordsRead = 0;` incremented per non-blank line. # gh-1073: Session JSONL grows unboundedly (12 GiB ledger records) → resume fails with 'Failed to read session' + heap-exhaustion crash

## Description

## Session file grows unboundedly (12 GiB) → resume fails with `SessionException: Failed to read session`, then Dart VM OOM crash

### Observed (live, 2026-09-29)

A month-long CLI session (`2026-09-07…01a07bce-….jsonl`) grew to **12.4 GiB / 96,776 lines**. Messages themselves are only ~17 MB; 99.9 % of the file is `custom` ledger records:

| customType | records | total | avg |
|---|---|---|---|
| `model_request_summary` | 18,753 | 9.08 GB | ~484 KB |
| `shell_job_registry` | 29,348 | 3.65 GB | ~124 KB |
| `subagent_registry` | 3,588 | 0.5 GB | ~140 KB |

Resuming the session fails:

```
error: failed to open session 01a07bce-…: SessionException: Failed to read session …/2026-09-07…_01a07bce….jsonl
```

and the process then crashes hard:

```
Exhausted heap space, trying to allocate 25575341936 bytes
```

### Root cause

1. **Unbounded append-only ledgers.**
   - `shell_job_registry` (`lib/src/cli/agent_hub_cli.dart`, `_persistJobBoard`): every job-board mutation appends a **full snapshot of all job cards** (commands, cwd, log tails). ~29k snapshots over the session lifetime; no cap, no dedup, no rotation.
   - `model_request_summary` (`lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`, `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_blobs.dart`): written before **every** model request and embeds a per-message summary of the whole outbound context (`messageCount` reached 1030+). Growth is superlinear: the longer the session, the bigger each record.

2. **Open path reads the whole file into one String.**
   `JsonlSessionStorage._openLocked` (`lib/src/session/session_storage.dart`) calls `fs.readTextFile(filePath)` on the entire JSONL. A 12.4 GiB UTF-8 file becomes a Dart UTF-16 `String` (~25 GB) → heap exhaustion; the wrapped `Failed to read session` error surfaces first, the retry then kills the VM.

   Note: faster/bounded parsing already exists (`SessionParseExecutor` header-only decode for big ledger payloads, `windowed_session_storage.dart`), but it only kicks in **after** the full-file `readTextFile`, so it cannot help here.

### Suggested fix directions

- **Streamed/windowed open**: read the JSONL line-by-line (or in bounded chunks) during open; never materialize the whole file as a single `String`. The header parse already only needs the first line.
- **Cap/rotate ledger records**:
  - `shell_job_registry`: keep only the latest snapshot (supersede prior records, e.g. tombstone/compact or a sidecar), or truncate job card payloads (log tails) before persisting.
  - `model_request_summary`: cap the per-message summary (max messages / max chars), and/or persist it only when the trajectory actually needs replay data.
- **Hard backstop**: refuse to full-read session files above a threshold (e.g. 1–2 GB) with a clear error pointing at a repair/`--shallow` resume path, instead of OOM-crashing.
- **Repair path**: a tool/command that rewrites a bloated JSONL, dropping or trimming `custom` ledgers, so users can rescue long-running sessions.

### Workaround for affected users

Copy the JSONL, strip `custom`-type lines (they are not needed to resume the conversation itself), and resume the copy — or start a new session.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/S…

All targeted tests green. Now deep review of the actual code for remaining issues. Let me examine full new files and relevant existing code:

1. `_scanSegmentStreamed` — check details:
   - `SessionLineScanner(fs: fs, path: segmentPath).scan(...)` — fine.
   - batchFirstLineNumber drift: minor.
   - Note: the rewrite copies good spans via decode/encode. OK.
   - `rewriteMs` set from `phaseSw.elapsedMilliseconds` which started at scan start — so rewriteMs includes read time. Minor reporting inaccuracy. Actually `readMs = phaseSw.elapsedMilliseconds` after flushBatch, then rewrite happens, and `rewriteMs = phaseSw.elapsedMilliseconds` — that's cumulative elapsed since scan start, not rewrite duration. Minor logging inaccuracy. Suggestion-level nit at best.

2. `_openStreamedLocked`: `latestGiantCustoms` — after the loop, full parse of each raw line via `parseSessionEntryLine(rawLine, filePath, 0)`. The line number arg 0 — parse errors would report line 0. Minor.

3. Backstop check for parts: per-segment 2 GiB. OK.

4. `defaultMaxFullOpenBytes = 2 << 30` — actually 2 GiB = 2147483648. `2 << 30` = 2 * 2^30 = 2 GiB. Yes.

5. `SessionLineScanner.scan` — `carry = BytesBuilder(copy: false)`; per-line `carry.toBytes()` then reassign. Fine. `carry.isNotEmpty` — BytesBuilder has isNotEmpty. OK.

6. Edge: a chunk boundary mid-line; sublist per line — O(n²)? `carry.add(chunk.sublist(lineStart, i))` copies; each line's bytes copied ~twice. For a 2 GiB file with small lines, chunk.sublist per line copies each byte once into carry, then toBytes copies again. Acceptable.

7. Performance concern: in `_scanSegmentStreamed`, the batch weight: `batchLines.fold<int>(0, (n, l) => n + l.length)` — O(batch) each line added → O(batch²) per batch ≈ 500² = 250k char-length ops per batch — fine.

8. `repairSessionLedgers`: After pass 1, `keptSpans.addAll(latestByType.values)` then sort. But `_appendSpan` coalesced keptSpans; adding latest spans after could create overlap? No — latest spans were excluded from keptSpans (returned before `_appendSpan`). Sorting gives file order. Correct.

   But wait — `recordsKept = keptSpans.length` — after coalescing; equals the count of kept lines only if spans are 1:1 with lines... `_appendSpan` merges contiguous spans, so keptSpans.length ≤ kept line count. recordsKept is thus the merged span count, not the record count. The report says "recordsKept" and summary prints "$recordsKept kept". Slightly inaccurate when contiguous lines coalesce (the common case! consecutive kept lines merge into one span). Hmm, actually let me re-check the scan callback: for kept lines it calls `_appendSpan(goodSpans, span)` — consecutive kept lines coalesce into a single span. So keptSpans.length undercounts records. `recordsRead` counts lines. So "records read: 10, kept: 3" could print when 10 records were read and 8 kept contiguously (one span). That's a real (cosmetic) reporting bug worth flagging. Let me verify: in `repairSessionLedgers`, `var recordsRead = 0;` incremented per non-blank line. Kept lines go through `_appendSpan(keptSpans, span)` — coalesced. So yes, recordsKept is span-count. In the dry-run summary "10 records read, 3 kept" would be wrong (8 actually kept).

   Wait, let me double check the test: seedSession writes header + 5 custom ledger lines + 1 message. Repair: all 5 customs dropped, message kept → keptSpans = [message span] → recordsKept = 1. recordsRead = 6? Summary line: "6 records read, 1 kept" — accurate there because dropped lines break contiguity. But in a dry-run of a healthy session with 100 contiguous message lines: recordsRead=100, kept=1 span. Report would say "1 kept". Misleading. Severity: IMPORTANT? It's a user-facing report accuracy issue in a brand-new command whose whole purpose is reporting. I'd say SUGGESTION-to-IMPORTANT. The dry-run report is what users use to decide. I'll classify as IMPORTANT-lite... Actually the counting is genuinely wrong for the primary use case (dry-run on a bloated file with mostly-kept conversation lines): "kept" would show tiny numbers. Users may misread "dropped" from recordsRead - recordsKept. I'll rate IMPORTANT.

   Hmm wait — actually let me recheck: are contiguous spans actually merged in repair? `_appendSpan(keptSpans, span)` — yes, merges when `spans.last.$2 == span.$1`. Consecutive kept lines → one span. So recordsKept == number of spans, not records. Confirmed bug (cosmetic but user-facing).

9. `_liveRowForPath` calls `repo.list()` — full listing; fine.

10. `session_repair_command.dart`: by-id path — `resolveRepairableSession` lists sessions and calls `repo.sessionNameQuick(metadata)` for each — check exists. Also note: by-id path does NOT verify the file exists before repair; repairSessionLedgers stats and fails with notFound — handled.

11. Live guard: presenceStore staleness — `list()` auto-drops stale heartbeats (15s). OK.

12. Repair + rotation: a session that has `.part-NN` segments! `repairSessionLedgers` repairs only the given path (primary). But the bloat may live in the rotated `.part-NN` segments (rotation moves older records into parts). The repair drops ledger records from the primary only; the parts still hold giant ledger lines. After repair, open loads parts oldest-first — still streams them (bounded), but the file size problem persists — the total across segments may still exceed 2 GiB, and the per-segment backstop only refuses > 2 GiB per segment. Total = parts + primary each < 2 GiB but sum > 2 GiB → open proceeds, streaming handles it (bounded memory). So not a memory issue, but the repair command's promise ("shrink the ledger") doesn't address parts: the giant ledger records in `.part-NN` files survive the repair and the session file set stays bloated. Does the error message "shrink the ledger with `fa session repair`" help when the primary is small but parts are huge? The tooLarge refusal only triggers per-segment. So a session whose primary is 100 MB but parts total 12 GiB never refuses and streams fine — bounded memory, just slow. Hmm, streaming 12 GiB in 4 MiB chunks = ~3000 reads — OK.

    But also: does repair consider that the LATEST shell_job_registry snapshot may live in a part segment? If the primary contains zero `shell_job_registry` records (all rotated to parts), repair keeps none, and resume rehydration finds nothing — job board empty. That's semantically fine (registry is best-effort). And model_request_summary in parts are replay-only. So acceptable, but worth a SUGGESTION: repair should mention/handle `.part-NN` siblings (at minimum warn that rotated segments were not scanned, or repair them too).

    Actually wait — is there a correctness issue? `fa session repair <id>` resolves the session primary path. Rotation parts are siblings `<path>.part-NN`. Repair doesn't touch them. Fine but incomplete w.r.t. the ticket's goal (the 12.4 GiB file had no rotation, probably). SUGGESTION.

If shallow parse said it's a valid custom record (header decoded), full parse should succeed too... unless the payload JSON is malformed but header fine. Then open throws SessionException — whole open fails where the whole-file path might have... the whole-file path parses all lines with parseSessionEntryLine too, failing similarly. Consistent.

Part files are `<primary>.part-0001` — they do NOT end in `.jsonl`, so the repair CLI's path branch (`target.endsWith('.jsonl')`) refuses... actually no — the by-id branch resolves metadata.path (primary). The path branch accepts only `.jsonl`-suffixed targets; a user cannot point repair at a `.part-NN` file via the CLI at all (`session repair: no such file` → actually it first checks `env.exists(target)` — the part exists, but since it doesn't end with `.jsonl` it goes to the by-id branch → "session not found"). So rotated segments can never be repaired via the CLI. A rotated session whose parts hold the bloat stays bloated, and the `tooLarge` error message points at `fa session repair` as the rescue path — which won't shrink the parts.

How severe? The tooLarge refusal fires per-segment (>2 GiB). If a `.part-NN` exceeds 2 GiB, the user is told to run `fa session repair`, which only rewrites the primary — the part remains > 2 GiB and open still refuses. The rescue path named in the error is a dead end for exactly that case. That's a functional gap worth IMPORTANT (docs/hint overpromise; also repair could iterate parts). Though — memory-wise the streamed open handles big-but-under-2GiB segments fine; the refusal is only per-segment >2GiB. The 12.4 GiB ticket session was a single unrotated file. Rotation only kicks in at kSessionSegmentRotateBytes — let me check the value.
{"command":"grep -n \"kSessionSegmentRotateBytes\" lib/src/session/session_storage.dart | head -3; sed -n 384,400p lib/src/session/session_storage.dart"}

Rotation caps segments at ~95 MB, so a `.part-NN` can never approach the 2 GiB backstop — per-segment refusal on parts can't realistically trigger. So the `tooLarge` refusal realistically only fires on the primary, and repair targets exactly the primary. The rotation-gap concern is thus minor: parts stay ≤95 MB each, total across many parts can be GiBs but the streamed open handles that in bounded memory. So repair ignoring parts means post-repair open still streams all parts — correct, just not smaller. The error hint remains valid for the realistic case. I'll downgrade this to a SUGGESTION (repair could optionally compact parts / note in help that rotated segments are untouched).

# gh-1073: Session JSONL grows unboundedly (12 GiB ledger records) → resume fails with 'Failed to read session' + heap-exhaustion crash

## Description

## Session file grows unboundedly (12 GiB) → resume fails with `SessionException: Failed to read session`, then Dart VM OOM crash

### Observed (live, 2026-09-29)

A month-long CLI session (`2026-09-07…01a07bce-….jsonl`) grew to **12.4 GiB / 96,776 lines**. Messages themselves are only ~17 MB; 99.9 % of the file is `custom` ledger records:

| customType | records | total | avg |
|---|---|---|---|
| `model_request_summary` | 18,753 | 9.08 GB | ~484 KB |
| `shell_job_registry` | 29,348 | 3.65 GB | ~124 KB |
| `subagent_registry` | 3,588 | 0.5 GB | ~140 KB |

Resuming the session fails:

```
error: failed to open session 01a07bce-…: SessionException: Failed to read session …/2026-09-07…_01a07bce….jsonl
```

and the process then crashes hard:

```
Exhausted heap space, trying to allocate 25575341936 bytes
```

### Root cause

1. **Unbounded append-only ledgers.**
   - `shell_job_registry` (`lib/src/cli/agent_hub_cli.dart`, `_persistJobBoard`): every job-board mutation appends a **full snapshot of all job cards** (commands, cwd, log tails). ~29k snapshots over the session lifetime; no cap, no dedup, no rotation.
   - `model_request_summary` (`lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`, `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_blobs.dart`): written before **every** model request and embeds a per-message summary of the whole outbound context (`messageCount` reached 1030+). Growth is superlinear: the longer the session, the bigger each record.

2. **Open path reads the whole file into one String.**
   `JsonlSessionStorage._openLocked` (`lib/src/session/session_storage.dart`) calls `fs.readTextFile(filePath)` on the entire JSONL. A 12.4 GiB UTF-8 file becomes a Dart UTF-16 `String` (~25 GB) → heap exhaustion; the wrapped `Failed to read session` error surfaces first, the retry then kills the VM.

   Note: faster/bounded parsing already exists (`SessionParseExecutor` header-only decode for big ledger payloads, `windowed_session_storage.dart`), but it only kicks in **after** the full-file `readTextFile`, so it cannot help here.

### Suggested fix directions

- **Streamed/windowed open**: read the JSONL line-by-line (or in bounded chunks) during open; never materialize the whole file as a single `String`. The header parse already only needs the first line.
- **Cap/rotate ledger records**:
  - `shell_job_registry`: keep only the latest snapshot (supersede prior records, e.g. tombstone/compact or a sidecar), or truncate job card payloads (log tails) before persisting.
  - `model_request_summary`: cap the per-message summary (max messages / max chars), and/or persist it only when the trajectory actually needs replay data.
- **Hard backstop**: refuse to full-read session files above a threshold (e.g. 1–2 GB) with a clear error pointing at a repair/`--shallow` resume path, instead of OOM-crashing.
- **Repair path**: a tool/command that rewrites a bloated JSONL, dropping or trimming `custom` ledgers, so users can rescue long-running sessions.

### Workaround for affected users

Copy the JSONL, strip `custom`-type lines (they are not needed to resume the conversation itself), and resume the copy — or start a new session.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),

All targeted tests green. Now deep review of the actual code for remaining issues. Let me examine full new files and relevant existing code:

1. `_scanSegmentStreamed` — check details:
   - `SessionLineScanner(fs: fs, path: segmentPath).scan(...)` — fine.
   - batchFirstLineNumber drift: minor.
   - Note: the rewrite copies good spans via decode/encode. OK.
   - `rewriteMs` set from `phaseSw.elapsedMilliseconds` which started at scan start — so rewriteMs includes read time. Minor reporting inaccuracy. Actually `readMs = phaseSw.elapsedMilliseconds` after flushBatch, then rewrite happens, and `rewriteMs = phaseSw.elapsedMilliseconds` — that's cumulative elapsed since scan start, not rewrite duration. Minor logging inaccuracy. Suggestion-level nit at best.

2. `_openStreamedLocked`: `latestGiantCustoms` — after the loop, full parse of each raw line via `parseSessionEntryLine(rawLine, filePath, 0)`. The line number arg 0 — parse errors would report line 0. Minor.

3. Backstop check for parts: per-segment 2 GiB. OK.

4. `defaultMaxFullOpenBytes = 2 << 30` — actually 2 GiB = 2147483648. `2 << 30` = 2 * 2^30 = 2 GiB. Yes.

5. `SessionLineScanner.scan` — `carry = BytesBuilder(copy: false)`; per-line `carry.toBytes()` then reassign. Fine. `carry.isNotEmpty` — BytesBuilder has isNotEmpty. OK.

6. Edge: a chunk boundary mid-line; sublist per line — O(n²)? `carry.add(chunk.sublist(lineStart, i))` copies; each line's bytes copied ~twice. For a 2 GiB file with small lines, chunk.sublist per line copies each byte once into carry, then toBytes copies again. Acceptable.

7. Performance concern: in `_scanSegmentStreamed`, the batch weight: `batchLines.fold<int>(0, (n, l) => n + l.length)` — O(batch) each line added → O(batch²) per batch ≈ 500² = 250k char-length ops per batch — fine.

8. `repairSessionLedgers`: After pass 1, `keptSpans.addAll(latestByType.values)` then sort. But `_appendSpan` coalesced keptSpans; adding latest spans after could create overlap? No — latest spans were excluded from keptSpans (returned before `_appendSpan`). Sorting gives file order. Correct.

   But wait — `recordsKept = keptSpans.length` — after coalescing; equals the count of kept lines only if spans are 1:1 with lines... `_appendSpan` merges contiguous spans, so keptSpans.length ≤ kept line count. recordsKept is thus the merged span count, not the record count. The report says "recordsKept" and summary prints "$recordsKept kept". Slightly inaccurate when contiguous lines coalesce (the common case! consecutive kept lines merge into one span). Hmm, actually let me re-check the scan callback: for kept lines it calls `_appendSpan(goodSpans, span)` — consecutive kept lines coalesce into a single span. So keptSpans.length undercounts records. `recordsRead` counts lines. So "records read: 10, kept: 3" could print when 10 records were read and 8 kept contiguously (one span). That's a real (cosmetic) reporting bug worth flagging. Let me verify: in `repairSessionLedgers`, `var recordsRead = 0;` incremented per non-blank line. Kept lines go through `_appendSpan(keptSpans, span)` — coalesced. So yes, recordsKept is span-count. In the dry-run summary "10 records read, 3 kept" would be wrong (8 actually kept).

   Wait, let me double check the test: seedSession writes header + 5 custom ledger lines + 1 message. Repair: all 5 customs dropped, message kept → keptSpans = [message span] → recordsKept = 1. recordsRead = 6? Summary line: "6 records read, 1 kept" — accurate there because dropped lines break contiguity. But in a dry-run of a healthy session with 100 contiguous message lines: recordsRead=100, kept=1 span. Report would say "1 kept". Misleading. Severity: IMPORTANT? It's a user-facing report accuracy issue in a brand-new command whose whole purpose is reporting. I'd say SUGGESTION-to-IMPORTANT. The dry-run report is what users use to decide. I'll classify as IMPORTANT-lite... Actually the counting is genuinely wrong for the primary use case (dry-run on a bloated file with mostly-kept conversation lines): "kept" would show tiny numbers. Users may misread "dropped" from recordsRead - recordsKept. I'll rate IMPORTANT.

   Hmm wait — actually let me recheck: are contiguous spans actually merged in repair? `_appendSpan(keptSpans, span)` — yes, merges when `spans.last.$2 == span.$1`. Consecutive kept lines → one span. So recordsKept == number of spans, not records. Confirmed bug (cosmetic but user-facing).

9. `_liveRowForPath` calls `repo.list()` — full listing; fine.

10. `session_repair_command.dart`: by-id path — `resolveRepairableSession` lists sessions and calls `repo.sessionNameQuick(metadata)` for each — check exists. Also note: by-id path does NOT verify the file exists before repair; repairSessionLedgers stats and fails with notFound — handled.

11. Live guard: presenceStore staleness — `list()` auto-drops stale heartbeats (15s). OK.

12. Repair + rotation: a session that has `.part-NN` segments! `repairSessionLedgers` repairs only the given path (primary). But the bloat may live in the rotated `.part-NN` segments (rotation moves older records into parts). The repair drops ledger records from the primary only; the parts still hold giant ledger lines. After repair, open loads parts oldest-first — still streams them (bounded), but the file size problem persists — the total across segments may still exceed 2 GiB, and the per-segment backstop only refuses > 2 GiB per segment. Total = parts + primary each < 2 GiB but sum > 2 GiB → open proceeds, streaming handles it (bounded memory). So not a memory issue, but the repair command's promise ("shrink the ledger") doesn't address parts: the giant ledger records in `.part-NN` files survive the repair and the session file set stays bloated. Does the error message "shrink the ledger with `fa session repair`" help when the primary is small but parts are huge? The tooLarge refusal only triggers per-segment. So a session whose primary is 100 MB but parts total 12 GiB never refuses and streams fine — bounded memory, just slow. Hmm, streaming 12 GiB in 4 MiB chunks = ~3000 reads — OK.

    But also: does repair consider that the LATEST shell_job_registry snapshot may live in a part segment? If the primary contains zero `shell_job_registry` records (all rotated to parts), repair keeps none, and resume rehydration finds nothing — job board empty. That's semantically fine (registry is best-effort). And model_request_summary in parts are replay-only. So acceptable, but worth a SUGGESTION: repair should mention/handle `.part-NN` siblings (at minimum warn that rotated segments were not scanned, or repair them too).

    Actually wait — is there a correctness issue? `fa session repair <id>` resolves the session primary path. Rotation parts are siblings `<path>.part-NN`. Repair doesn't touch them. Fine but incomplete w.r.t. the ticket's goal (the 12.4 GiB file had no rotation, probably). SUGGESTION.

13. In `_openLocked`, the stat retry: `retryTransientSessionIo(() => fs.fileInfo(filePath), op: 'open', ...)`. Then for the streamed path, primaryFileSize is passed. Between the heal and the stat — heal ran before stat. Good ordering as documented.

14. `_openStreamedLocked` — after scanning, it fully parses latest giant customs. Note: `parseSessionEntryLine(rawLine, filePath, 0)` — could throw on a malformed giant line (it was parsed shallow OK but full parse fails?). If shallow parse said it's a valid custom record (header decoded), full parse should succeed too... unless the payload JSON is malformed but header fine. Shallow decode uses `parseShallowCustomRecord` which checks the header; the full decode could fail on bad payload JSON. Then open throws SessionException — whole open fails where the whole-file path might have... the whole-file path parses all lines with parseSessionEntryLine too, failing similarly. Consistent.

15. Timing: `parseMs` only counts giant-custom rehydration; batch parsing happens inside flushBatch during scan (counted in readMs window since phaseSw covers scan until readMs snapshot). Mislabeled but harmless.

16. `agent_hub_cli.dart` `_persistJobBoard`: `_persistChain.then((_) async {...})` — with `on Object` catch inside?…

How severe? The tooLarge refusal fires per-segment (>2 GiB). The rescue path named in the error is a dead end for exactly that case. That's a functional gap worth IMPORTANT (docs/hint overpromise; also repair could iterate parts). So the `tooLarge` refusal realistically only fires on the primary, and repair targets exactly the primary. The rotation-gap concern is thus minor: parts stay ≤95 MB each, total across many parts can be GiBs but the streamed open handles that in bounded memory. So repair ignoring parts means post-repair open still streams all parts — correct, just not smaller. The error hint remains valid for the realistic case. # gh-1073: Session JSONL grows unboundedly (12 GiB ledger records) → resume fails with 'Failed to read session' + heap-exhaustion crash

## Description

## Session file grows unboundedly (12 GiB) → resume fails with `SessionException: Failed to read session`, then Dart VM OOM crash

### Observed (live, 2026-09-29)

A month-long CLI session (`2026-09-07…01a07bce-….jsonl`) grew to **12.4 GiB / 96,776 lines**. Messages themselves are only ~17 MB; 99.9 % of the file is `custom` ledger records:

| customType | records | total | avg |
|---|---|---|---|
| `model_request_summary` | 18,753 | 9.08 GB | ~484 KB |
| `shell_job_registry` | 29,348 | 3.65 GB | ~124 KB |
| `subagent_registry` | 3,588 | 0.5 GB | ~140 KB |

Resuming the session fails:

```
error: failed to open session 01a07bce-…: SessionException: Failed to read session …/2026-09-07…_01a07bce….jsonl
```

and the process then crashes hard:

```
Exhausted heap space, trying to allocate 25575341936 bytes
```

### Root cause

1. **Unbounded append-only ledgers.**
   - `shell_job_registry` (`lib/src/cli/agent_hub_cli.dart`, `_persistJobBoard`): every job-board mutation appends a **full snapshot of all job cards** (commands, cwd, log tails). ~29k snapshots over the session lifetime; no cap, no dedup, no rotation.
   - `model_request_summary` (`lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`, `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_blobs.dart`): written before **every** model request and embeds a per-message summary of the whole outbound context (`messageCount` reached 1030+). Growth is superlinear: the longer the session, the bigger each record.

2. **Open path reads the whole file into one String.**
   `JsonlSessionStorage._openLocked` (`lib/src/session/session_storage.dart`) calls `fs.readTextFile(filePath)` on the entire JSONL. A 12.4 GiB UTF-8 file becomes a Dart UTF-16 `String` (~25 GB) → heap exhaustion; the wrapped `Failed to read session` error surfaces first, the retry then kills the VM.

   Note: faster/bounded parsing already exists (`SessionParseExecutor` header-only decode for big ledger payloads, `windowed_session_storage.dart`), but it only kicks in **after** the full-file `readTextFile`, so it cannot help here.

### Suggested fix directions

- **Streamed/windowed open**: read the JSONL line-by-line (or in bounded chunks) during open; never materialize the whole file as a single `String`. The header parse already only needs the first line.
- **Cap/rotate ledger records**:
  - `shell_job_registry`: keep only the latest snapshot (supersede prior records, e.g. tombstone/compact or a sidecar), or truncate job card payloads (log tails) before persisting.
  - `model_request_summary`: cap the per-message summary (max messages / max chars), and/or persist it only when the trajectory actually needs replay data.
- **Hard backstop**: refuse to full-read session files above a threshold (e.g. 1–2 GB) with a clear error pointing at a repair/`--shallow` resume path, instead of OOM-crashing.
- **Repair path**: a tool/command that rewrites a bloated JSONL, dropping or trimming `custom` ledgers, so users can rescue long-running sessions.

### Workaround for affected users

Copy the JSONL, strip `custom`-type lines (they are not needed to resume the conversation itself), and resume the copy — or start a new session.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/S…

Long AGENTS.md. The key conventions relevant: god-file ceiling 2800 lines, grouped append-only barrel exports, part file patterns.
